# dsh-llm-dump

Captures **every complete LLM request** and stores it folded: repeated message
prefixes and large re
peated fields are stored once and referenced by hash.

- Hook: the `llm/stream` waterfall. The listener observes `GenerateOptions` and
never modifies it, s

o capture cannot change what the model receives.
- No `fetch` interception is involved: the full req

uest object is available at
this seam, so prefix matching is a local computation over captured paylo

object is available at
this seam, so prefix matching is a local computation over captured payloads.

This is a host-side bundle with no browser half. It needs a DeepSeek Harness
build that provides the

side bundle with no browser half. It needs a DeepSeek Harness
build that provides the `llm` service.

## What is captured
`GenerateOptions` at the provider boundary:

- `messages` — the full model-visible conversation, including the assembled
system prompt
- `tools`

— active tool definitions
- `model`, `provider`, `sessionId`, sampling fields
- `toolHistory` and ot
her large top-level fields (stored once, referenced)

Adapters may still transform the request afterwards (image projection, tool
updates, deferred loadin
g); this is the last public state before that step.

same session and list

Each record also carries `sha1`, the hash of the whole request's canonical JSON,
so a replay can pro
ve it reconstructed the exact content.
## Data format (version 1)

`requests.jsonl` and `responses.jsonl` are an append-only contract shared with
dsh-dump-manager. Rea

ders
must ignore unknown fields so a later minor version can add them.

The format number is advertised as `dsh.formatVersion` in this package's
`package.json` (currently `

1`), independently of the package's semver — a
UI-only release does not look like a format change. `

dsh-dump-manager` reads it
at startup and warns when it cannot read what this writer produces.
| File | One line per | Fields |

| `objects.jsonl` | unique content | `h` (SHA-1 of canonical JSON), `v` (the value) |
| `requests.js
onl` | request | `at`, `seq`, `sessionId`, `provider`, `model`, `messageCount`, `toolCount`, `prefix

Len`, `suffix`, `tools`, `top`, `sha1` |
| `responses.jsonl` | finished stream | `seq`, `request` (t
he request `sha1`), `at`, `ms`, `reason`, `usage`, `blocks`, `interrupted` |

- `messages` is stored only through `suffix`; `prefixLen` says how much of the
previous request's me

ssage list is reused.
- `top` holds every other top-level field. A value larger than 1 KB is replace

d
by `{"$dshRef": "<hash>"}` and stored once in `objects.jsonl`; `tools` uses the
same indirection (

or `null` when the request had no tools).
- Hashes are SHA-1 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no wh

itespace), the same
computation `tools/unfold-dump.mjs --verify` repeats.
## Response capture

Requests alone cannot show the newest answer: the reply to request *n* only
enters the dump when req

uest *n+1* resends it as an `assistant` message. The
listener therefore also reads the stream it is

forwarding and appends one line to
`responses.jsonl` when the stream ends:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- Blocks are assembled with the harness's own rules, duplicated here because a
plugin cannot import

the internal package: deltas per index, `block-end`
overrides, `max-tokens` drops tool calls, an int

errupted stream keeps only
closed text/reasoning.
- `interrupted` is true when no `finish` chunk arr

ived (consumer cancelled) or
the finish kind is `error` / `aborted`; the record then holds exactly w

hat was
delivered before the cut.
- Capture is observation only: every chunk is forwarded unchanged,

the upstream
iterator is closed when a consumer stops early, and no error can escape into
the respo

ream
iterator is closed when a consumer stops early, and no error can escape into
the response path.

Every response is stored, but they are mostly redundant — all except the newest
one reappear inside

the next request. `dsh-dump-manager` shows only the newest,
which is the one the request snapshots c

`dsh-dump-manager` shows only the newest,
which is the one the request snapshots can never contain.

`DSH_LLM_DUMP_CONFIG` overrides the config path.

`dsh-dump-manager` can edit this file from its settings page; unknown keys are

## Replay
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`--verify` recomputes the canonical hash of every replayed request and fails on
any mismatch. The to

ol reads `outputDir` from the same config file, so it works
against any capture directory.
## Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Both tests run in a throwaway `DSH_HOME` under the system temp directory and
never touch the real pr

ests run in a throwaway `DSH_HOME` under the system temp directory and
never touch the real profile:

- `test/smoke-fold.mjs` — prefix reuse, one object per unique value, and a replay
whose canonical ha

sh matches every record.
- `test/smoke-response.mjs` — chunk forwarding, block assembly, the `seq` /
`sha1` link back to the request, and an aborted stream.
## Privacy

The dump holds the entire model-visible conversation, including file contents,
tool output, and the

system prompt. Keep it out of repositories and delete it
when the investigation ends.
